senses: A famous red-stone mountain in Guangdong; namesake of Danxia landform.
Red sandstone landform with sheer cliffs, named by Chen Guoda in the 1930s.
Nickname for Danxia Mountain: hundreds of red peaks like ruby sculptures.
Rock formation along Jinjiang River resembling elephants wading.
Hill silhouette of a sleeping girl, viewed from Yangyuan Bridge.
Famous phallic stone column on Yangyuan Hill (~28m high, ~7m diameter).
Cliff formation paired with Yangyuan; nature’s “Adam and Eve” motif.
Temple built in 1662 (Kangxi year 1); one of northern Guangdong’s great monasteries.
Kaiping watchtower-style buildings combining defense, residence, and Sino-Western art.
Finest residential diaolou in Zili Village; built 1925, five storeys.
Highest and most luxurious Kaiping tower; nine storeys, ~25m.
Typical watchtower (1920) with generator, searchlights, and guns.
Chinese–Western villa garden in Tangkou; built 1936 by Xie Weili.
“Cultivating moral character is the foundation of success” — Li Garden motto.
Society for the Revival of China; founded by Sun Yat-sen in Honolulu, 1894.
China Revolutionary League (1905); later the Nationalist Party / Guomintang.
Architect of Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall; Cornell-trained; died 1929 aged 36.
Second king of Nanyue; styled himself Emperor Wen; reigned 137–122 BC.
Former Qin general who founded the Nanyue Kingdom at the start of Western Han.
Set of eight bronze chimes from Nanyue (129 BC); still playable after 2,100+ years.
Clansman who won tanhua (third place) in 1893; reason for the temple’s stone drums.
Third place in the imperial palace examination.
Homophonic relief: bird, deer, bee, monkey — wishing titles, salary, and nobility.
Highest imperial examination degree; families with jinshi or above could place stone drums.
Honorific for the Chen Family Temple / Chen Clan Academy.
